accede

ak-SEED · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To accede is to agree to a demand, request, or treaty.

After months of tense negotiation, both governments finally agreed to accede to the new trade treaty.

Example

The landlord eventually acceded to the tenants' request for working heat, though only after a formal complaint was filed.

Formally agreeing to a specific, named request -- working heat -- after a formal process is exactly what accede describes.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

consent: To consent is to give permission -- you allow something to happen, often something done to you or around you. To accede is to say yes to a demand or request that someone has pressed on you, usually after a process or a negotiation. Consent grants permission; accede answers a demand.

assent: Assent is expressing approval of a plan or statement -- a nod, a signed line, a spoken yes. Accede goes a step further: you give in to a specific demand or request, often one you first resisted. You assent to ideas; you accede to demands.

acquiesce: To acquiesce is to stop resisting and let a thing go forward without ever voicing agreement -- reluctance is built in. Accede is the more active, procedural word: you actually agree to the demand, request, or treaty put to you. Silence gives way in one; a stated yes in the other.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

refuse: indicate unwillingness to do something

reject: dismiss as inadequate or unacceptable

Where it sits · how much ground is given up — allow → accede → capitulate

allow vs. accede: To allow something is simply to permit it; to accede is to formally agree to a specific demand or request, often after negotiation.

capitulate vs. accede: Capitulate goes further than accede, suggesting a total surrender of position rather than a single formal agreement.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — ac-

prefix — ac-: toward (Latin (ad-))

root — ced

root — ced: to go, yield (Latin (cedere))

suffix — -e

suffix — -e: verb-forming ending (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Ac- ('toward') plus ced- ('to go, yield') gives 'to go toward, yield to' -- to accede is to formally give way to a specific request.

Use the root in a new word: concede

Use the root in a new word: concede: After a week of back-and-forth, the airline finally conceded on the refund.

Word Choice

Accede is the more plain, procedural cousin of "acquiesce" (this same unit) -- it names a formal agreement to a specific request or treaty, without necessarily implying reluctance or exhaustion.
